properties.name: Hardknott Pass
properties.reason: Single-track, severe hairpins and gradients around 1 in 3. Penfold can physically fit, but the LWB/tight steep turns make this an avoid-by-default road.

properties.name: Wrynose Pass
properties.reason: Narrow mountain road with steep gradients and hairpins. Doable in a T6-sized camper, but reversing/passing can be awkward.

properties.name: Honister Pass
properties.reason: Very steep and narrow in sections with tourist, bus, cycle and walking traffic.

properties.name: Newlands Pass
properties.reason: Tight in places with very steep sections and limited passing. Much less pleasant at busy times.

properties.name: Kirkstone Pass (A592)
properties.reason: Steep and occasionally narrow, but a normal through-road and substantially easier than Hardknott/Wrynose.

properties.name: Porlock Hill (A39)
properties.reason: Very steep with hairpins. Penfold should be capable, but the toll road is the lower-stress alternative.

properties.name: Winnats Pass
properties.reason: Steep, narrow and often busy with walkers/cyclists. Penfold fits, but timing matters.

properties.name: Rosedale Chimney Bank
properties.reason: Extremely steep with difficult alignment. Not a sensible Penfold through-route.

properties.name: Bwlch y Groes
properties.reason: Very narrow, severe gradients and little room. Possible, but little upside in an LWB camper unless the drive itself is the objective.

properties.name: Gospel Pass
properties.reason: Long stretches of single-track, steep sections and winter exposure. Good in settled weather if you are happy reversing.

properties.name: Black Mountain Pass (A4069)
properties.reason: Twisty and exposed but a proper A-road. Generally a good Penfold scenic route in normal weather.

properties.name: Bealach na Bà
properties.reason: Single-track, steep drops and tight hairpins. Penfold is within the sensible VW-camper size bracket, but confident reversing is essential.

properties.name: B869 Drumbeg Road
properties.reason: Very narrow single-track with bends and crests. Penfold is small enough, but long reversing is a realistic possibility.

properties.name: Quiraing road
properties.reason: Single-track with passing places and a tight switchback. Vehicle size is fine; peak-season congestion is the bigger issue.

properties.name: Applecross coastal road
properties.reason: Long single-track stretches but fewer extreme hairpins/gradients than Bealach na Bà.

properties.name: Glen Etive road
properties.reason: Long dead-end single-track road. Penfold fits; congestion and meeting traffic are the issue.

properties.name: Duke's Pass (A821)
properties.reason: Very twisty with elevation changes, but normal road width for most of its length.

properties.name: B3306 St Ives–Zennor
properties.reason: Tight coastal B-road with narrow sections. Penfold-sized vans are normal, but summer traffic can make it a squeeze.

properties.name: Hemmick Beach access lane
properties.reason: Very steep, narrow approach with horseshoe bends and virtually no turning room. Campervan/motorhome reports describe vehicles struggling to climb back out.

properties.name: Sutton Bank (A170)
properties.reason: Very steep signed hill with a sharp bend. Penfold is far smaller than an HGV, but this deserves more respect than a normal A-road.

properties.name: Buttertubs Pass
properties.reason: Narrow exposed moorland road with steep sections, bends and limited passing. Suitable for a capable campervan driver but not a carefree shortcut.

properties.name: Fleet Moss / Oughtershaw road
properties.reason: High, narrow and exposed with steep approaches and single-track sections. Weather and meeting traffic matter more than Penfold's absolute dimensions.

properties.name: Tan Hill approach roads
properties.reason: Remote high moorland roads, generally achievable in Penfold but narrow/exposed and potentially difficult in poor weather.

properties.name: The Struggle, Ambleside–Kirkstone
properties.reason: Very steep alternative approach to Kirkstone with bends and narrow sections. Doable, but not the relaxed way to get Penfold up to the pass.

properties.name: Hawkshead–Coniston minor-road corridor
properties.reason: Known for narrow walled sections and awkward encounters with buses/large traffic. Penfold fits, but expect patience and occasional reversing.

properties.name: Wasdale Head approach
properties.reason: Long narrow approach with stone walls and meeting-traffic pressure. Penfold-sized vehicles are practical, but progress can be slow.

properties.name: Langdale / Blea Tarn road
properties.reason: Narrow, steep and twisty minor road connecting Great Langdale toward Wrynose. Treat as an intentional scenic drive rather than a normal route.

properties.name: Abergwesyn Pass / Devil's Staircase
properties.reason: Remote single-track mountain road with a famously steep hairpin section. Penfold can fit, but visibility, gradient and reversing are the issue.

properties.name: Elan Valley mountain road
properties.reason: Narrow scenic reservoir/mountain road with bends and occasional single-track character. Generally Penfold-friendly with sensible speed.

properties.name: Llanberis Pass (A4086)
properties.reason: Main road but constrained by rock faces, parking pressure, buses and tourist traffic. Penfold fits comfortably; congestion is the real concern.

properties.name: Pen-y-Pass / Nant Gwynant (A498)
properties.reason: Mountain A-road with bends, buses and visitor traffic. Normally suitable for Penfold, but parking/congestion can make it feel tighter.

properties.name: Machynlleth–Llanidloes mountain road
properties.reason: Remote minor-road crossing with narrow sections and little traffic. A good example of a route where Penfold fits but Google-style shortcuts deserve scrutiny.

properties.name: Cwmystwyth mountain road
properties.reason: Narrow remote valley road with limited passing and exposed sections. Generally manageable in a Transporter-sized camper.

properties.name: Vale of Ewyas / Capel-y-ffin road
properties.reason: Very narrow rural valley road with constrained passing before/around Gospel Pass. Fine if quiet; awkward when busy.

properties.name: Mam Rat / Rushup Edge minor road
properties.reason: Steep/narrow Peak District minor-road territory adjacent to Winnats; worth treating cautiously in a long-wheelbase camper.

properties.name: Snake Pass (A57)
properties.reason: Twisty and exposed but a normal A-road. Penfold suitability is generally good; weather and closures are more important than size.

properties.name: Woodhead Pass (A628)
properties.reason: Strategic trans-Pennine route used by substantial commercial traffic. Default green for Penfold unless a temporary restriction applies.

properties.name: Cat and Fiddle (A537)
properties.reason: Fast, exposed, bend-heavy A-road. No inherent Penfold dimensional problem; use normal mountain-road care.

properties.name: Achnashellach–Torridon (A890/A896)
properties.reason: Highland road with narrower sections and single-track character in places. Penfold is a sensible size for it; passing-place etiquette matters.

properties.name: Shieldaig–Applecross coastal road
properties.reason: Single-track scenic route with passing places. Longer and slower than a normal road but generally a good Penfold option.

properties.name: Kinloch Hourn road
properties.reason: Long dead-end single-track road with remote, narrow sections. Penfold fits, but meeting traffic can mean significant reversing.

properties.name: Mallaig–Morar old/minor roads
properties.reason: Some narrow local roads around the coast/beaches; main A830 is green-quality, but satnav diversions onto minor lanes deserve caution.

properties.name: Ardnamurchan B8007
properties.reason: Long single-track road with many passing places. Slow rather than inherently unsuitable; Penfold is a very reasonable vehicle for it.

properties.name: Mull B8035 west coast
properties.reason: Classic island single-track road. Penfold fits; patience, passing places and avoiding convoy behaviour are the key issues.

properties.name: Mull Calgary–Dervaig road
properties.reason: Narrow island road with passing places. Normal territory for Transporter-sized campers but not fast travel.

properties.name: Skye Elgol road (B8083)
properties.reason: Long narrow single-track road with blind bends and tourist traffic. Penfold is suitable, but reversing skill and patience are important.

properties.name: Skye Glen Brittle road
properties.reason: Single-track dead-end access with heavy visitor traffic for the Fairy Pools/Glen Brittle area. Congestion is the principal Penfold problem.

properties.name: Loch Arkaig road
properties.reason: Long narrow dead-end loch road with limited passing. Penfold fits but can require substantial reversing when traffic meets.

properties.name: Loch Etive north-shore access
properties.reason: Remote minor-road access where narrowness and turning opportunities matter. Investigate destination/turning point before committing.

properties.name: Durness–Kinlochbervie (A838/B801)
properties.reason: Remote single-track/highland-road sections but designed for local traffic. Penfold is a sensible size; use passing places correctly.

properties.name: Kylesku–Drumbeg alternative A894
properties.reason: The lower-stress strategic alternative when you do not fancy the B869 Drumbeg road. Default good Penfold route.

properties.name: Cheddar Gorge (B3135)
properties.reason: Narrow/bendy scenic gorge with rock faces and visitor traffic, but routinely used by vans and buses. Penfold fits; take bends slowly.

properties.name: Countisbury Hill (A39)
properties.reason: Steep coastal A-road. Penfold has no unusual size issue, but descents/climbs deserve lower gears and sensible braking.

properties.name: Valley of Rocks / Lynton local road
properties.reason: Narrow scenic local road with constrained sections and visitor traffic. Worth checking your exact route rather than following a satnav blindly.

properties.name: Dartmeet–Postbridge (B3212)
properties.reason: Moorland B-road with bends, livestock and tourist traffic. Normally comfortable enough for Penfold.

properties.name: Widecombe–Haytor minor road
properties.reason: Narrow rural moorland road, but generally manageable in a Transporter. Use care around stone walls and meeting traffic.

properties.name: Hartland Quay approach
properties.reason: Steep/narrow coastal approach where turning and meeting traffic can be awkward. Penfold-sized but worth deliberate route choice.

properties.name: Clovelly approach/local lanes
properties.reason: The main visitor approach is manageable; surrounding local lanes can be much tighter. Stay on the signed access route.

properties.name: Zennor–St Just B3306
properties.reason: Spectacular but bendy/narrow coastal B-road. Penfold is a normal-sized vehicle here; summer meeting traffic is the challenge.

properties.name: King Harry Ferry approach lanes
properties.reason: Ferry itself accommodates vehicles, but local approach roads can be narrow. Penfold is practical if you stay on signed routes.

properties.name: Lizard peninsula minor coastal lanes
properties.reason: Highly variable Cornish lanes: some are easy, others hedge-bound and effectively single-track. Unknown until the exact road is assessed.

properties.name: Gower Rhossili approach (B4247)
properties.reason: Main approach is suitable for Penfold but can be busy/narrow-feeling in summer. Avoid opportunistic satnav diversions onto tiny lanes.

properties.name: Gower Oxwich local approach
properties.reason: Local lanes can be very narrow and constrained by hedges/walls. Penfold can fit, but route selection matters.

properties.name: Newgale–Solva coastal road (A487)
properties.reason: Coastal A-road with bends and seasonal traffic but fundamentally suitable for Penfold.

properties.name: St Davids minor coastal lanes
properties.reason: Road quality varies sharply away from the A487. Treat unsurveyed coastal lanes as unknown rather than assuming campervan suitability.

properties.name: Bwlch-y-Groes alternative A494 corridor
properties.reason: Main-road alternative to committing to the much more severe Bwlch y Groes minor-road crossing.

properties.name: A82 Glencoe
properties.reason: Strategic trunk route used by coaches and HGVs. Default green for Penfold; weather/incidents can still override that.

properties.name: A9 Highland trunk route
properties.reason: Major strategic trunk road. Default green for Penfold unless a specific temporary restriction applies.

properties.name: A30 Cornwall trunk route
properties.reason: Primary strategic route into Cornwall. Default green and preferable to satnav shortcuts through hedge-bound lanes.

properties.name: A55 North Wales Expressway
properties.reason: High-standard strategic route. Default green for Penfold subject to signed/temporary restrictions.

properties.name: A591 Kendal–Keswick
properties.reason: Main Lake District arterial route; handles motorhomes routinely. Default green for Penfold unless a temporary restriction applies.

properties.name: Windermere west-shore road
properties.reason: Narrower in places than the eastern-shore routes, especially around Ferry Nab. Penfold is workable but meeting traffic deserves care.

properties.name: A39 Bude–Newquay
properties.reason: Straightforward main-road Cornwall corridor with regular passing opportunities; preferable to minor-lane satnav shortcuts.

properties.name: A38 South-east Cornwall
properties.reason: Main strategic route and generally unproblematic for campervans.

properties.name: A390 Cornwall corridor
properties.reason: Main south-Cornwall route; substantially preferable to unsigned/minor alternatives for Penfold.

properties.name: Porthcurno approach lanes
properties.reason: Cove approach roads can be extremely narrow with steep gradients and tight bends. Route choice and peak-season traffic matter.

properties.name: Kynance Cove approach
properties.reason: Narrow coastal access; campervan guidance specifically flags smaller cove approaches as roads where larger vehicles should take care.

properties.name: Cadgwith approach lanes
properties.reason: Fishing-village approach with very narrow local lanes. Penfold is compact for a camper, but this is still deliberate-route territory.

properties.name: Mousehole approach from Newlyn
properties.reason: Tight turns and granite-wall constraints make the village approach awkward for larger vehicles; use the main signed approach only.

properties.name: Port Isaac local approach
properties.reason: Local lanes are exceptionally tight; use designated visitor access/parking rather than driving toward the historic centre.

properties.name: Polperro local approach
properties.reason: Historic village roads are challenging for larger vehicles. Use signed visitor routes and parking rather than centre-bound satnav instructions.

properties.name: Mevagissey local approach
properties.reason: Constrained fishing-village streets and seasonal congestion. Main signed approach is preferable; avoid tiny centre lanes.

properties.name: Fowey local approach
properties.reason: Reachable by sensible main approaches, but town-centre streets are much less camper-friendly. Use designated parking.

properties.name: B3311 / Halsetown approach to St Ives
properties.reason: Frequently cited as problematic in peak season, when parked cars further constrain an already awkward approach.

properties.name: Hirnant Pass / Lake Vyrnwy–Bala route
properties.reason: Narrow with passing places, but motorhome users report it suitable for vehicles short of coach-sized. Penfold is well within that scale.

properties.name: A470 Cambrian Way trunk sections
properties.reason: Principal north-south road through much of Wales. Default green for Penfold; minor scenic deviations are assessed separately.

properties.name: A835 Inverness–Ullapool
properties.reason: Major NC500 approach/strategic road. Default green for a Transporter-sized camper.

properties.name: A836 north-coast NC500
properties.reason: Much is manageable Highland road, but single-track sections and passing-place etiquette justify yellow rather than blanket green.
